newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower as seasonal slowdown bites.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower as seasonal slowdown bites.

text.p: COMEX copper ended sharply weaker for the second day running as funds and speculators continued to sell amid rising stocks in the summer slowdown, traders said.

"It continues to be mostly technical and fund driven," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said. "With stocks increasing and demand likely to contract over the next couple of months, there is not much support in the market right now."
Most-active September COMEX copper settled 2.55 cents weaker at 102.50 cents a lb, traded 104.70 to 101.50 cents. Spot July went out 2.35 cents lower at 105.05 cents.
September copper has fallen from a recent high of 119.65 cents - its close on June 18 - to its lowest since April 16.
A key underpinning to prices, the LME cash to three months backwardation, eased to $110/$118 a tonne, down $10/$15 from Tuesday's COMEX close.
LME stocks continue to rise, up 975 tonnes Wednesday to 134,325 tonnes, partly due to influx of COMEX stocks.
U.S. physical merchants said more copper was expected to flow from COMEX warehouses to their U.S LME counterparts because of the LME premium over COMEX in nearby months.

Rinehimer said a key to recovery in prices was the hope that China would be lured in to buy. "If these prices trigger some increase in Chinese buying, then it could hold above a dollar (per lb) level and turn back up," he said.
The market continued to shrug off production outages as the seasonal slowdown in Europe and the U.S. began to bite the order books.
Sterlite Industries' 100,000 tonne a year copper smelter in India has been shut down since Sunday. The temporary closure was ordered by the authorities because of a suspected gas leak.
Activity at the Neves Corvo copper mine in southern Portugal was paralysed for the third day running Wednesday as miners continued to strike over working hours.
